Why scale by √d?

By A. Writer · 3 min read

Dot products of random vectors grow with their dimension — roughly like √d. See the variance post & notes.

A quick check

import numpy as np
q, k = np.random.randn(2, 512)

print(q @ k)  # about sqrt(512) in size

Things to remember:

  • Mean is 0.
  • Variance is d.
    • So the std is √d.
  1. Third
  2. Fourth

Softmax saturates when its inputs are large.

Prices like $5 and 2*3 and snake_case stay literal.

Inline TeX from MathJax: \(\sqrt{d_k}\) and a display one: \[\sum_i q_i k_i\]

1. Not a list, just a sentence that starts with a number.
